newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: World Bank economist chides Latin America.
newsitem.headline: World Bank economist chides Latin America.

text.p: The World Bank's top Latin American economist chided the region Tuesday for its inefficient banking and financial sectors, inconsistent fiscal policies and a lack of market openness compared with other parts of the world.

"In almost all indicators, Latin America is far behind Asia and the industrialized world" in terms of efficient administration of public revenues, said Guillermo Perry, World Bank chief economist for Latin America and the Caribbean, said at a banking conference in Buenos Aires.

Regarding budget balancing, "fiscal adjustment is not guaranteed yet in Latin America" despite reforms at the national level, he said, because many countries have failed to bring their provincial governments up to date and are carrying heavy deficit burdens.
"In my opinion, this will have to be confronted by countries like Argentina and Brazil in the next 10 years," Perry told the conference.
